idiom_name: select with a default branch on a channel send/receive
implementation_notes: Go's idiom for balking is a select with a default branch: the send or receive is attempted, and when it cannot proceed right away the default case runs and the operation is abandoned instead of blocking the goroutine - the spec states that the default case is chosen when no other case can proceed. The channel *is* the state (a full buffer or an absent receiver is exactly the 'not right now' predicate), which removes the classic monitor-plus-flag structure and keeps every mutation in one goroutine. Choose this form when the guarded resource is a channel or a permit; reach for sync.Mutex.TryLock only when the protected state is inherently shared memory.
pitfalls: A select with only nil channels and no default case blocks forever instead of balking - never use nil channels as the guard.
Sending on a closed channel panics; closing the guard channel is not how the pattern signals 'not now', it is how producers end a stream.
select/default tests channel readiness, not arbitrary struct state: if the predicate is a field, all its mutations must still go through one goroutine or a mutex.

variants.name: sync.Mutex.TryLock (shared-memory guard)
variants.implementation_notes: sync.Mutex.TryLock - added in Go 1.18 - reports whether the lock was acquired without blocking, giving the shared-memory version of the pattern: take the mutex, read the state, return early when it forbids the action, otherwise transition and unlock. Pick it when the guarded state is a plain struct shared by goroutines rather than a channel; Go's own guidance favours channels for coordination, so treat TryLock as the exception and prefer select/default unless the state genuinely cannot be expressed as ownership of a channel.
pitfalls: TryLock must be paired with Unlock only when it returned true; unlocking an unheld mutex panics.
TryLock ignores waiting goroutines, so a starving waiter is possible by design - use Lock when the caller must eventually proceed.
Copying a struct that embeds a sync.Mutex (passing Machine by value) breaks the lock; guarded types must be used through pointers.
